titre: Exercices — La modalité : déduction, reproche et regret (should have…)
consigne: Cherche chaque exercice au brouillon avant d'ouvrir le corrigé.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must, might ou can't : « His car isn't here, so he ___ be at home. »
corrige: Absence d'un indice attendu → conclusion sûre négative.
On emploie can't : he can't be at home.

exercices.enonce: Exprime une simple possibilité : « The door is unlocked. Someone ___ (to be) inside. »
corrige: Hypothèse non certaine → might/may/could.
Someone might be inside.

exercices.enonce: Transpose au passé : « He looks pale. He ___ (to see) a ghost! »
corrige: Déduction sûre sur un fait passé → must have + PP.
He must have seen a ghost!
exercices.reponse: He must have seen a ghost!

exercices.enonce: Exprime l'impossibilité passée : « You ___ (to finish) already — you only started five minutes ago! »
corrige: Certitude négative sur le passé → can't have + PP.
You can't have finished already.

exercices.enonce: Formule un reproche : « The meeting was important, but Tom didn't come. → Tom ___ . »
corrige: Action attendue non faite → should have + PP.
Tom should have come.

exercices.enonce: Exprime un regret : « I told her the secret. Now I regret it. → I ___ . »
corrige: Action qu'on n'aurait pas dû faire → shouldn't have + PP.
I shouldn't have told her the secret.
exercices.reponse: I shouldn't have told her the secret.

exercices.enonce: Emploie needn't have : « I cooked a huge dinner, but nobody was hungry. → I ___ so much. »
corrige: Effort passé rendu inutile → needn't have + PP.
I needn't have cooked so much.
exercices.reponse: I needn't have cooked so much.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec mustn't ou don't have to : « Passengers ___ lean out of the window. » et « You ___ pay, it's on me. »
corrige: Interdiction → mustn't.
Absence d'obligation → don't have to.
exercices.reponse: Passengers mustn't lean out of the window. / You don't have to pay, it's on me.

exercices.enonce: Emploie could have : « The accident was avoided by luck. → Someone ___ (to be) killed. »
corrige: Conséquence grave possible mais non réalisée → could have + PP.
Someone could have been killed.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Elle a dû rater son train ; elle aurait dû partir plus tôt. »
corrige: « a dû rater » = déduction passée → must have missed.
« aurait dû partir » = reproche → should have left.
exercices.reponse: She must have missed her train; she should have left earlier.
